citations.A1: the cache has an initialization guard, not an invalidation policy — `_cache is None` is only ever true once per process, so disk changes can never be seen; fix by recording the file's identity stamp
citations.A2: **Not a fix — TTL/expiry:** it only bounds how long you serve stale data instead of removing the staleness
citations.A3: **Not a fix — dropping the cache and reading every call:** it does end the staleness but discards the caching the function exists to provide
citations.A4: one global slot is shared across all `path` values, so the first caller's file is returned to every other caller forever; fix by keying the cache dict on the resolved absolute path
citations.A5: Concurrent first-callers can each open and parse the file and race on the global assignment; fix with a module-level `threading.Lock`
